issues.legal_issue: A court may impose terms when allowing an application to set aside an ex parte decree, but those terms must not be unreasonable or so onerous that they prejudge the merits or effectively decide the suit.
material_facts: The applicants sought to set aside ex parte decrees and explained the delay in bringing their applications.
The trial court condoned the delay but required the applicants to deposit the entire amounts claimed in the suits.
The suits had not been decided on their merits, and the applicants had not yet had an opportunity to contest them.
The applicants deposited a lesser amount pursuant to an interim order of the Supreme Court.
issues.conclusion: The condition requiring deposit of the entire suit claims was unreasonable and onerous and was set aside. The ex parte decrees were set aside and the suits restored for trial; the amount already deposited was to be invested for the benefit of whichever party ultimately succeeded.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order IX Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure, a court exercising discretion to set aside an ex parte decree may put the defendant on terms, including payment of costs or part of the decretal amount, but the terms must not be unreasonable, harshly excessive, or have the effect of prejudging the suit. Tea Auction Limited v. Grace Hill Tea Industry and Vijay Kumar Madan v. R.N. Gupta Technical Education Society establish these limits; the same view was reiterated in V.K. Industries v. M.P. Electricity Board.

rule.if: ex_parte_set_aside_proceeding and (delay_satisfactorily_explained and merits_undecided) and entire_claim_deposit_required

predicates.ex_parte_set_aside_proceeding: A defendant applied to set aside an ex parte decree and sought condonation of delay in making the application.
predicates.delay_satisfactorily_explained: The defendant satisfactorily explained the reasons for the delay in applying to set aside the decree.
predicates.merits_undecided: The underlying suit had not yet been decided on its merits, leaving the defendant without an opportunity to contest it.
predicates.entire_claim_deposit_required: The court required the defendant to deposit the entire amount claimed in the suit as a condition of setting aside the decree.

issues.definition: When a defendant satisfactorily explains delay in an application to set aside an ex parte decree and the suit remains undecided on its merits, requiring deposit of the entire claim as a condition is invalid.

issues.legal_issue: Delay in applying to set aside an ex parte decree should be condoned when the applicant satisfactorily explains it and the circumstances do not establish negligence, inaction, or lack of bona fides.
material_facts: The applicants sought condonation of delays of 355 and 382 days in filing their applications to set aside ex parte decrees.
They stated that they learned of the decrees when they saw a public notice concerning attachment of the property.
The Supreme Court found that the applicants had satisfactorily explained the reasons for the delay.
issues.conclusion: The delay in filing the applications to set aside the ex parte decrees was condoned.
issues.legal_principle: Section 5 of the Limitation Act requires sufficient cause for condonation of delay. The expression ‘sufficient cause’ is to be construed liberally to advance substantial justice where negligence, inaction, or lack of bona fides is not attributable to the applicant; the discretion must be exercised judicially, with vigilance and circumspection, and the applicant’s due diligence is the relevant test.

predicates.ex_parte_set_aside_proceeding: A defendant applied to set aside an ex parte decree and sought condonation of delay in making the application.
predicates.delay_satisfactorily_explained: The defendant satisfactorily explained the reasons for the delay in applying to set aside the decree.
predicates.applicant_negligent_or_inactive_or_not_b: The defendant was negligent or inactive, or acted without bona fides, in pursuing the application.

issues.definition: Delay in an application to set aside an ex parte decree is condoned when the defendant satisfactorily explains it and was not negligent or inactive and did not lack bona fides.
